title: Sevilla vs. Barcelona: Barça Lineup Changes for the Big Match
seoTitle: Sevilla vs Barcelona: Barça Lineup Changes
subtitle: Hansi Flick makes four changes and starts Livakovic in goal
excerpt: For the clash against Sevilla, Hansi Flick made four changes to Barcelona's XI, featuring Livakovic's start in goal and adjustments in defense and attack.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Sevilla and Barcelona took center stage after head coach Hansi Flick announced four changes to the side set to face the opposition at the Sánchez Pizjuán. The headline change was Livakovic starting in goal, replacing Szczesny, who dropped to the bench following a mistake against Racing.

Livakovic takes over in goal

Any doubt over who would guard Barcelona's goal was settled with Livakovic making his starting debut. The replacement for Joan Garcia was chosen following the performance of Szczesny, whose error led to a goal against Barça in the previous matchday.

Defense gets a new look

In the backline, Eric Garcia retains his starting spot for the third consecutive game. On the left flank, Cancelo remains at full-back after contributing with goals in the previous match against Racing. The central defense features Cubarsí, who returns to the starting lineup, alongside Christensen, who also keeps his place.

Midfield led by Rodri and Pedri

The playmaking department remains in the hands of the Rodri-Pedri duo, who established themselves as starters ever since the clash against Valencia. Marc Bernal awaits an opportunity to feature, staying on the bench alongside other substitutes.

Options on the wing and in attack

In the attacking midfield role, Fermín replaces Olmo, who played in the previous game against Racing. On the left wing, Gordon and Adeyemi rotate, with Gordon handed the start. Lamine remains untouched on the right, while Raphinha continues as the central attacker, maintaining his steady goalscoring form.

Substitutes' bench

Alongside the starters, the bench features Szczesny (backup goalkeeper), Iker Rodríguez, Balde, Koundé, Espart, Gerard Martín, Bernal, Adeyemi, Gavi, and Hamza, ready to step in should the manager make changes during the match.

With information from Mundo Deportivo.
